'''''Viburnum lantana''''', the '''wayfarer''' or '''wayfaring tree''', is a species of ''[[Viburnum]]'', native to central, southern and western [[Europe]] (north to [[Yorkshire]] in [[England]]), northwest [[Africa]], and southwestern [[Asia]].<ref name=fe>[http://rbg-web2.rbge.org.uk/cgi-bin/nph-readbtree.pl/feout?FAMILY_XREF=&GENUS_XREF=Viburnum+&SPECIES_XREF=lantana&TAXON_NAME_XREF=&RANK= Flora Europaea: ''Viburnum lantana'']</ref><ref name=blamey>Blamey, M. & Grey-Wilson, C. (1989). ''Flora of Britain and Northern Europe''. {{ISBN|0-340-40170-2}}</ref><ref name=rhs>Huxley, A., ed. (1992). ''New RHS Dictionary of Gardening''. Macmillan {{ISBN|0-333-47494-5}}.</ref> The vigorous deciduous European treelike shrub is common along waysides.

==Description==
It is a [[deciduous]] [[shrub]] or small [[tree]] growing to {{convert|4–5|m|abbr=on}} tall. The [[leaf|leaves]] are opposite, simple oval to lanceolate, {{convert|6 - 13|cm||abbr=on}} long and {{convert|4–9|cm|abbr=on}} broad, with a finely serrated margin; they are densely downy on the underside, less so on the upper surface. The [[plant sexuality|hermaphrodite]] [[flower]]s are small, around {{convert|5|mm|abbr=on}}, and creamy-white, produced in dense [[Cyme (botany)|cymes]] {{convert|4–10|cm|abbr=on}} width at the top of the stems; they are produced in early summer, and [[pollination|pollinated]] by [[insect]]s. The [[fruit]] is an oblong [[drupe]] {{convert|8|mm|abbr=on}} long, green at first, turning red, then finally black at full maturity, and contains a single [[seed]]. The seeds are dispersed when [[bird]]s eat the fruit, then deposit the seeds in another location in their droppings.<ref name=blamey/><ref name=rhs/>

An older name for the plant is '''hoarwithy'''. "Hoar" means grey-haired and refers to the hairs under the leaves, and "[[withy]]" means a pliant stem.<ref>Reader's Digest Field Guide to the Trees and Shrubs of Britain ''p.87''.</ref>

[[File: Wolliger Schneeball mit zeitgleich roten unreifen und schwarzen reifen Früchten.jpg |thumb|right|Showing simultaneous red (unripe) and black (ripe) fruits]]

==Cultivation and uses==
It is commonly grown as an [[ornamental plant]] for its flowers and berries, growing best on [[alkali soils|alkaline soils]]. A number of [[cultivar]]s have been selected, including 'Aureum', with yellow leaves in spring.<ref name=rhs/>

The fruit is of low to zero toxicity, but may cause vomiting or diarrhea if consumed unripe or in large quantities.<ref name=pfaf>[[Plants for a Future]]: [http://www.pfaf.org/user/Plant.aspx?LatinName=Viburnum%20lantana ''Viburnum lantana'']</ref>
